problems.wrong: The envelope holds three things: the card number and the {{term:ksn}} in the clear, and the locked PIN block.
problems.right: The envelope holds five things: a trace id, the card number and the KSN in the clear, the locked PIN block, and a seal (a CMAC) over all of them.
problems.evidence: PinEnvelope.cs fields: version, traceId, pan, ksn, lockedPinBlock, mac. Step S07 already says the gateway sees the trace id, and S10 says the bank checks a seal on the whole envelope.

problems.wrong: It passes through four hands: the PIN pad, the old device (the CE), the gateway, and the server. The bank checks it last.
problems.right: It passes through five parts: the PIN pad, the old device (the CE), the gateway, the server, and the bank.
problems.evidence: Lesson 9 names doc: five processes (reader, ce, gateway, server, bank); S09 says the server hands the envelope to the bank.

problems.wrong: The reply is one result byte and a code, with no seal on it.
problems.right: The reply is one result byte and a code, with no end-to-end seal on it. It rides inside the sealed hops, but the CE cannot check where it came from.
problems.evidence: BankReply.Build has no MAC; the reply passes back through the SSH and TLS channels.

notes: Every try-it behaves as written: L9-tamper-hop1 fails packet MAC at the gateway, L9-tamper-hop2 fails AEAD tag at the server, L9-flip-pin-block passes both hop checks and fails at the bank.
